title: Traffic Fabric for Simultaneous Shadow + Live A/B with Hierarchical Signaling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and deliver a lightweight orchestration layer that allows a single route to serve live traffic, shadow requests, and run A/B exposures in parallel. The fabric should support hierarchical statistical signaling (request -> cohort -> global) for early-stop, progressive exposure, and policy-driven auto-revert.
background: Current rollout tooling supports simple cohort splits and canaries but lacks an integrated way to run shadow trials alongside live A/B traffic while surfacing per-cohort statistical signals and drift. Teams end up creating ad-hoc pipelines or duplicating traffic; this increases cost and slows iteration. We need a composable fabric that minimizes runtime overhead while providing robust multi-metric checks and exposure budgets.
proposal: Build a Traffic Fabric service that sits in the request plane and provides three coordinated capabilities: 1) deterministic split routing for live A/B exposures (per-request hashing), 2) sampled shadowing with configurable amplification and async capture, and 3) hierarchical signal aggregation that evaluates metrics at request, cohort, and global levels using Bayesian sequential tests and drift detectors. Expose a single declarative experiment spec (YAML/JSON) that defines arms, exposure budgets, stop criteria, and data sinks for evaluations. The fabric will integrate with Console for visualization and with the Optimize engine for adaptive exposure suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment spec applied to a route successfully splits 0-100% traffic deterministically across arms
Shadowed requests are delivered asynchronously to a target model and stored without impacting live latency (tail latency regression <1%)
Hierarchical signals (request -> cohort -> global) are computed and show Bayesian early-stop recommendations within 5 minutes of significant divergence for high-impact metrics
Auto-revert policy can be configured per-experiment and triggers rollback when defined thresholds are hit
Console shows exposure timelines, cohort-level metrics, and recommended actions; API returns experiment status and recommended exposure adjustments
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement core routing and shadow plumbing (ENG). Phase 2: Integrate sequential Bayesian test and drift detector (ML/Research). Phase 3: Console UI + API + RBAC and policy controls (Product/Design). Phase 4: Beta with two internal teams, collect feedback, iterate on thresholds and UX. Phase 5: Public release with docs and runbook.
metrics: primary: relative regression in downstream NPS-like quality signal (per-request correctness proxy)
latency: p50/p95/p99 tail delta between baseline and experiment arms
cost: tokens-per-inference and calls-shadowed amplification ratio
safety: rate of safety guard triggers per 1000 requests
drift: distributional shift score (KL / Wasserstein approximations) per cohort
statistical_tests: Bayesian sequential test on primary metric with Bayes factor thresholds for early-stop
Cohort-level permutation tests for edge-case regressions
Drift detector based on streaming two-sample test with exponential decay weighting
Multiple-hypothesis correction via hierarchical testing at cohort->global aggregation
exposure_policy: Declarative policy supports: max_absolute_exposure, ramp_schedule (linear, stepped), minimum_sample_before_eval, safety_budget (metric-specific thresholds), and adaptive_backoff (reduce exposure by factor on weak signals). Policies can pin to dedicated capacity tiers or fall back to cheaper quantized variants.
risks: Cost of shadowing at scale if amplification is misconfigured
False early-stops from noisy proxies without adequate sample size
Increased operational complexity if team-level experiment specs diverge from org standards
Potential data leakage to shadow destinations if not properly isolated
notes: Implementation should prefer async shadow delivery and use reservoir sampling for high-throughput routes. Consider a lite client-side SDK for deterministic hashing to make split decisions stable across upstream proxies. Coordinate with Security for audit logging and with Dedicated team for capacity reservations when experiments pin to dedicated pools. Add canary for the fabric itself (start with internal-only routes).
